message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas – A Quick Reference Guide** | Topic | Key Points | Where to Find More Info | |-------|------------|------------------------| | **Speed Limits** | • General limit: 55 mph on rural roads, 45 mph on urban roads.
• 70 mph on interstate highways (except where posted otherwise).
• 65 mph on freeways in urban areas. | Texas Department of Transportation (TxDOT) – Speed Limit Guidelines | | **Seat‑belt & Child‑Safety** | • All occupants must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child safety seat or booster.
• No “seat‑belt law” for drivers over 18, but all passengers must buckle. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **Cell‑Phone Use** | • Hand‑held phone use while driving is prohibited (unless using a hands‑free system).
• Texting while driving is illegal. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) of 0.08% or higher is illegal.
• Zero‑tolerance for drivers under 21 (BAC ≥ 0.02%).
• Penalties include fines, license suspension, and possible jail time. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **Right‑of‑Way** | • Yield to pedestrians at crosswalks.
• Stop at red lights and stop signs.
• “Move‑over” law: vehicles must change lanes or slow down when approaching stopped emergency vehicles. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **School Bus Rules** | • Stop for a school bus with its stop sign extended and lights flashing.
• Vehicles must stop on both sides of the road. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **Headlights & Lighting** | • Headlights must be on from sunset to sunrise, and during any weather that reduces visibility.
• Fog lights may only be used when visibility is less than 200 ft. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **Towing & Tow‑away** | • Towing of a vehicle requires a valid towing permit.
• Tow‑away of a vehicle without a permit can result in fines. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **Parking Regulations** | • No parking within 20 ft of a fire hydrant.
• No parking in a driveway or on a private property without permission.
• Parking in a handicap space requires a valid handicap placard. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **Vehicle Registration & Inspection** | • All vehicles must be registered and display a valid license plate.
• Vehicles must pass an annual safety inspection (except for certain exempt categories). | Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (TxDMV) | | **Insurance Requirements** | • Minimum liability coverage: $30,000 for bodily injury per person, $60,000 for bodily injury per accident, $25,000 for property damage. | TxDMV – Insurance Requirements | | **Special Situations** | • “No‑stop” zones: no stopping, standing, or parking.
• “No‑left‑turn” zones: no left turns allowed.
• “No‑right‑turn” zones: no right turns allowed. | TxDOT – Roadway Signage Standards | --- ### How to Stay Updated 1. **Texas Transportation Code** – The official legal text governing all traffic laws. 2. **TxDOT Website** – Offers updates on road conditions, speed limits, and construction projects. 3. **TxDMV** – Provides information on registration, insurance, and driver licensing. 4. **Local County Courts** – For recent case law or changes in local ordinances. --- ### Quick Tips for Safe Driving in Texas - **Always keep your seat belt fastened** – it’s the single most effective way to reduce injury. - **Avoid distractions** – put your phone on “Do Not Disturb” mode while driving. - **Observe posted speed limits** – they’re designed for safety and can vary widely. - **Respect school bus rules** – stopping for a school bus is mandatory. - **Check your insurance** – ensure you meet the minimum liability requirements. Feel free to ask if you need details on a specific law, recent court cases, or how to handle a particular driving scenario!
